description: Al2219 element count and mesh convergence study
evidence: Rezwan (2025 intragranular) Sec. 2.4 gives only the dimensionless MOOSE mesh-density parameters (1 at the boundaries, 0.65 around the void), HEX8 elements and linear Lagrange shape functions. No element count, no element size, no convergence study anywhere in the paper.

The binding constraint is the phase-field one: with l = 1 um the usual h <= l/2 requirement implies element size <= 0.5 um in the damage-active region, so the mesh study must be run at FIXED l, not at fixed h/l.

Carry over eta = 1e-3 s/um and k = 1e-3 from the Al2219 deck as the starting point, converting eta to the mm system (1e-6 s/mm), and declare the carry-over as an assumption. evidence: Rezwan (2026 predicting) reports 9880 HEX8 elements in the gage region with spline-interpolated thickness, and no convergence study.

description: Mapping between the papers' SSD parameters (k_m or k_0, y_c) and a Kocks-Mecking storage/recovery pair (k1, k2)
evidence: Al2219 Eq. (12): rho_dot_SSD^a = (k_m*sqrt(rho) - 2*y_c*rho_SSD^a) * gamma_dot^a / b. Comparing with the Kocks-Mecking form rho_dot = k1*sqrt(rho)*gamma_dot - k2*rho*gamma_dot gives k1 = k_m / b and k2 = 2*y_c / b, with rho in Eq. (11) being the latent-hardened sum and rho_SSD^a the per-system self density. Numerically for Al2219: k1 = 0.3432 / 0.000286 um = 1200.0 um^-1 exactly (which suggests k_m was itself chosen to make k1 a round 1200 um^-1) and k2 = 2*0.00268 / 0.000286 = 18.741 (dimensionless). For Ni: k1 = 0.0295 / 2.5e-7 mm = 1.180e5 mm^-1 and k2 = 2*0.79e-6 / 2.5e-7 = 6.320. CRITICAL: the Ni paper's Eq. (10) prints the annihilation term as (2/y_c)*rho_SSD, which is dimensionally impossible (L^-3 against L^-1); the Al2219 form 2*y_c*rho_SSD is the dimensionally consistent one and is the form used for this mapping.
action_required: Verify the derived k1, k2 against PINNACLE's dislocation_density_cp implementation term by term before any calibration run, including which density (self vs latent-hardened sum) each term consumes. Confirm the sign and factor of 2 conventions. Re-derive if PINNACLE normalizes by b internally.

description: Third Euler angle (rotation about the loading axis) for the four extreme Al2219 orientations
evidence: Rezwan (2025 intragranular) Sec. 3.1.1 names the loading-axis directions [001], [101], [111] and [1bar 4 9] = (-1,4,9) but never specifies the rotation about that axis. Immaterial under the uniaxial BC (traction-free lateral faces), but NOT immaterial under the isochoric BC, which prescribes compression on both reciprocal directions and therefore couples to the in-plane orientation.
action_required: Fix one convention (e.g. minimum-rotation from the reference frame, or align the second sample axis with the lowest-index in-plane crystal direction), document it in the deck, hold it constant across all runs, and run a third-angle sensitivity study under the isochoric BC for all four orientations.

description: Time unit of the reported initial time step 0.045
evidence: NEW GAP (not in the companion sheet). Both papers give an initial time step of 0.045 with an adaptive stepper, and neither states the time unit. In a rate-dependent CP model with gamma_dot_0 = 1e-5 1/s, the absolute time scale sets the achieved strain rate, so the unit matters.
action_required: Infer the time unit from the applied displacement rate needed to reach the reported strain levels, state the inferred value, and verify that the resulting strain rate is quasi-static. Do not carry 0.045 across unit systems without this step.

description: Whether the density in Eq. (10)/(7) is the per-system self SSD density or the latent-hardened sum of Eq. (11)/(8)
evidence: NEW GAP (not in the companion sheet; it is what makes the sheet's own 43.6 MPa check ambiguous). Eq. (11) defines rho as sum_b chi^ab (rho_SSD^b + |rho_eGND^b| + |rho_sGND^b|). Evaluated at the initial state with chi = 1 on the diagonal and q = 1.4 off it over 12 FCC systems, rho_eff = 220.0 * (1 + 11*1.4) = 3608 um^-2 and the Taylor term becomes 176.60 MPa, a factor sqrt(1+11q) = 4.050 above the 43.61 MPa obtained from rho = rho0_SSD alone. The companion sheet's 43.6 MPa check therefore corresponds implicitly to the self term only.
action_required: Resolve by matching the initial yield point of the digitized Fig. 3 calibration curve (elastic-plastic knee at roughly 0.4-0.6 % strain and 135-345 MPa in the polycrystal aggregate) against both readings, and adopt the one that reproduces it. Record the decision in the deck; it moves the initial CRSS between 43.7 and 176.7 MPa.

description: Cross-material transferability of Gc (22.75 J/m^2 for Al2219 vs 1.25e5 J/m^2 for Ni)
evidence: NEW GAP (not in the companion sheet, which reports both values without flagging the gap). Al2219 Gc = 22.75 MPa-um = 22.75 J/m^2; Ni Gc = 125 kJ/m^2 = 125 MPa-mm. The ratio is 5495. A physical fracture energy for either FCC metal would be O(1e3-1e4) J/m^2, so the Al2219 value is a brittle-ceramic-scale number and both are effective calibration parameters rather than measured toughnesses. The phase-field driving force scales with Gc/l, and the Ni l_0 is unreported (gap C.3), so the two numbers are not directly comparable.
action_required: Never transfer Gc between the two decks. Calibrate Gc per material against its own experiment, and report the calibrated Gc together with the l_0 it was calibrated at, since only the pair is meaningful. Include Gc in the parameter-sensitivity stage for both materials.
